category: scholarly metadata API (works, authors, sources, institutions) and bulk snapshot

free_tier.stated: USD 1 of API usage a day with a free key: 10,000 list-and-filter calls, 1,000 searches or 100 content downloads, single-entity lookups unlimited; USD 0.10 a day with no key; the budget resets every midnight UTC
free_tier.notes: The budget is priced per call: a list or filter call costs USD 0.10 per 1,000, a search USD 1 per 1,000, a content download USD 10 per 1,000. A keyless list call on 2026-10-30 answered X-RateLimit-Limit 1000, X-RateLimit-Limit-USD 0.1 and X-RateLimit-Credits-Used 1, so the keyless day is 1,000 list calls.

per_object_cap.stated: per_page maximum 100 results; basic paging stops at 10,000 results, and cursor paging past the first page needs a free key; snapshot part files hold up to 400,000 records each

retention.stated: the API is a live index; the free public snapshot is a quarterly release on the second Wednesday of January, April, July and October (latest 2026-10-14); a daily snapshot is a Member+ plan benefit

egress.terms: The API is metered in credits per day, not in bytes. The public snapshot bucket s3://openalex is free to download with no AWS account; the AWS Open Data program covers the transfer, about USD 70 per full download.
egress.free_allowance: no byte cap published on the snapshot bucket

interface_detail: REST at https://api.openalex.org (GET, JSON; a key as the api_key query parameter or an Authorization: Bearer header); the snapshot in the public S3 bucket s3://openalex under data/jsonl/ (gzip JSON Lines) and data/parquet/, read anonymously with --no-sign-request or over HTTPS, each format with a manifest.json
tooling: curl or any HTTP client for the API; aws s3 sync with --no-sign-request (parallel and resumable) for the snapshot; DuckDB reads the gzip JSONL or Parquet part files directly
chaining: The S3 snapshot is the bulk path: about 626 million records, about 745 GB compressed as JSON Lines (works alone about 615 GB) or about 770 GB as Parquet, refreshed quarterly; the API at USD 1 a day with a free key covers lookups and the drift between releases, while the daily snapshot and changed-since-any-date filters are Member+ (USD 10,000 a year) benefits.

limits.value: no key: 10 requests a second; free key or prepaid usage: 30; annual plan: 50
daily budget: USD 0.10 with no key, USD 1 with a free key (10,000 list-and-filter calls or 1,000 searches or 100 content downloads); single-entity lookups free; resets every midnight UTC
per_page maximum 100; basic paging limit 10,000 results; cursor paging past the first page needs a free key

binding_note: The daily credit budget runs out first: a free key buys 10,000 list calls of up to 100 results, about 1,000,000 records a day, so a full copy comes from the snapshot, not the API.

identity_cost.detail: The API answers with no key at USD 0.10 a day, and the snapshot bucket needs no account. The free key comes from a sign-up form that asks for a name and an email address behind a CAPTCHA, or from a POST to https://api.openalex.org/api-keys with an email address; the key works only once its email address is verified. No payment method required.

reliability_note: Exceeding the daily budget or the per-second limit answers 429; a per-second 429 costs nothing and clears on retry.
confidence_note: The budget, rates, paging limits and snapshot sizes are vendor pages read on 2026-10-30; a keyless list call and a HEAD of the snapshot manifest were probed the same day and answered 200 with the keyless budget in the headers. No key was requested, so the keyed rate is documented only.
